page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine configured with a reduced memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-speed local NVMe storage. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, the instance delivers 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores via hyperthreading. Hardware resources include 64.0 GB of system memory (yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU), an expansive 480 MB L3 cache, and 1890 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The processor integrates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 extensions (VNNI, BF16) and Intel AMX (tile and int8), facilitating optimized vector and matrix operations without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements place the instance among top-performing hardware in vector math, text compression, and inference execution. It achieves 2191.0 in Geekbench single-core and 17995.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside strong scores in gzip compression (35.44 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (202.24 GB/sec multi-threaded). Thanks to AMX and AVX acceleration, the instance achieves top-tier results in text processing (Geekbench 2884.0) and small-model LLM text generation (346.08 tokens/sec on a 135M model), alongside strong prompt processing across small and medium parameter models. Standard integer stress-ng throughput and database operation benchmarks fall in the middle 50% percentile.

With its 1:2 memory-to-core ratio and 1890 GB NVMe drive, the primary architectural tradeoff centers on capacity versus computation. Workloads requiring large in-memory working sets may be bounded by the 64.0 GB limit, but applications requiring fast local scratch storage and robust compute density benefit from the platform's execution efficiency. The D32lds_v7 is well suited for static web serving, high-throughput compression pipelines, CPU-based machine learning inference, CI/CD compilation, and caching layers requiring dedicated CPU resources.
description: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring a 4.2 GHz dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking a GPU, it relies on modern CPU instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions to accelerate compute tasks. Benchmark results demonstrate strong performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, high-throughput data compression, static web serving (54.89 GB/sec), and small-model LLM inference, reaching top-tier rates for text processing. Memory capacity is constrained to 2.0 GB per vCPU, establishing a configuration geared toward high compute and fast disk caching rather than massive memory footprints. The instance fits high-throughput web serving, build automation, CPU-driven inference pipelines, and compression-heavy data tasks.
